numberItems.stem: With Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives, you must never park within how many feet of the traveled part of the road?
numberItems.explanation: Never park explosives within 5 feet of the traveled part of the road; 300 feet is the distance from bridges, tunnels, buildings, crowds and open fires (p. 9-16).

numberItems.stem: With Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives, you must not park within how many feet of a bridge, tunnel or building (except brief stops such as fueling)?
numberItems.explanation: Don't park explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather or open fire, except for brief stops such as fueling (p. 9-16).

numberItems.stem: A placarded vehicle that is NOT carrying explosives must not be parked within how many feet of an open fire?
numberItems.explanation: Every placarded vehicle must stay at least 300 feet from an open fire when parked; 25 feet is the no-smoking distance (p. 9-16).

numberItems.stem: If you are not in the vehicle, what is the farthest you may be from a placarded vehicle and still be attending it (with it in clear view)?
numberItems.explanation: The attendant must be in the vehicle awake (not in the sleeper) or within 100 feet of it with a clear view (p. 9-16).

numberItems.stem: [CA] In private carriage (not for hire), CHP explosives routes apply when you carry how much Division 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.6 explosives?
numberItems.explanation: In California, CHP routes apply to more than 1,000 pounds of these explosives in private carriage; any amount triggers them only for hire or delivery service (p. 9-17).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Hauling Division 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.6 explosives for hire, how much triggers the CHP special routes and stopping places?
numberItems.explanation: For hire or as a delivery service, any amount of these explosives must use CHP's special routes; the 1,000-pound limit is for private carriage (p. 9-17).

numberItems.stem: You must not smoke within how many feet of a placarded Class 3 (flammable liquid) cargo tank?
numberItems.explanation: No smoking within 25 feet of a placarded Class 3 or Division 2.1 cargo tank, or of any vehicle carrying Class 1, 3, 4.1, 4.2 or 5 (p. 9-18).

numberItems.stem: When a HazMat vehicle must stop at a railroad crossing, how far from the nearest rail should it stop?
numberItems.explanation: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail, then cross only when no train is coming and you can clear the tracks without stopping (p. 9-19).

numberItems.stem: After a crash involving explosives, you remove them before separating the vehicles. At least how far away must you place them?
numberItems.explanation: Place removed explosives at least 200 feet from vehicles and occupied buildings (p. 9-21).

numberItems.stem: How much estimated property damage from a HazMat incident requires a call to the National Response Center?
options: Only if a vehicle is a total loss
numberItems.explanation: The property-damage trigger is estimated damage of more than $50,000, not any damage (p. 9-22).

numberItems.stem: A HazMat incident forces the public to evacuate. The National Response Center must be called if the evacuation lasts:
numberItems.explanation: An evacuation of the general public for more than 1 hour is a reportable event (p. 9-22).

numberItems.stem: A liquid marine pollutant is released. Above what quantity must the National Response Center be called?
numberItems.explanation: The marine pollutant trigger is more than 119 gallons for liquids or 882 pounds for solids (p. 9-22).

numberItems.stem: What is the 24-hour toll-free number of the National Response Center?
numberItems.explanation: The National Response Center is 1-800-424-8802; 1-800-424-9300 is CHEMTREC (p. 9-22).

numberItems.stem: Carriers must send a detailed written report of a HazMat incident within:
numberItems.explanation: Carriers must make detailed written reports within 30 days of an incident (p. 9-22).
CHEMTREC is 1-800-424-9300 and gives crews technical HazMat facts; 1-800-424-8802 is the National Response Center (p. 9-22).
